answer: To open a voting seat, an operator must fund a one-way courier voyage that delivers a uniquely serialized marble to a staffed oasis depot, then lock 2,200 units for 18 days. The depot publishes a signed receipt and a close-up of the intact serial; a reused route, cloned stone, or shared payment rail slashes the bond. An honest applicant pays about $22 for one courier run and parks 2,200 units. Fielding 150 aliases needs 150 distinct stones and 330,000 units left idle, plus about $3,300 in courier fees, more than a typical council stipend can repay.
